Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) in Washington D.C. is searching for a Mission Support Specialist to support DELTA 13 (NH-0343-03, GS-12/13 Equivalent). Description: Step to the leading edge of national defense and help architect the future of the United States Space Force. In this high-impact strategic role, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge space and cyber operations and the Pentagon's resource allocation engine. Your expertise will directly shape how the Space Force organizes, educates, and resources its total force-translating advanced operational concepts in Space Domain Awareness, Space ISR, and multi-domain warfare into fully funded, actionable programs across the Program Objective Memorandum (POM) and Future Years Defense Program (FYDP). Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate is a seasoned human capital strategist, academic program manager, or military space operations professional with extensive headquarters-, Field Command-, or Delta-level staff experience in Total Force management and specialized Administratively Determined (AD) personnel systems. They possess deep expertise in the DoD Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process to build, defend, and integrate Space Force education, faculty pay requirements, and human capital initiatives into the Program Objectives Memorandum (POM) and Future Years Defense Program (FYDP). Additionally, they bring proven capability in administering complex AD faculty personnel actions, managing academic selection boards, and synchronizing requirements across Space Delta 13, STARCOM, and higher headquarters. Key Responsibilities: 1. Coordinates end-to-end personnel lifecycle actions for Administratively Determined (AD) Faculty, including recruitment, hiring authorities, salary determinations, appointments, contract extensions, onboarding, in/out-processing, and performance management across Senior Level Education programs. Serves as the primary personnel liaison between faculty, academic leadership and Space Delta 13. 2. Applies Department of Defense Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) processes to forecast, formulate, and execute faculty personnel and operational budgets. Develops Program Objectives Memoranda (POM) inputs, Budget Estimate Submissions (BES), cost projections, financial exhibits, and FYDP personnel projections/offsets for Delta 13 education programs. 3. Synchronizes personnel actions and operational alignment for Joint military instructors, Active Duty Guardians, and Total Force personnel assigned to or augmenting Space Force educational programs. Tracks suspense management, program records, and cross-service instructor memorandums of agreement (MOAs/MOUs). 4. Integrates Space Delta 13 faculty footprint, academic facility requirements, and classroom technology requirement. 5. Develops and standardizes Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), governance charters, business rules, and administrative tracking systems for the emerging Space Force education enterprise. Coordinates high-level academic meetings, faculty symposiums, and Distinguished Visitor (DV) engagements. 6. Analyzes complex programmatic, personnel, and fiscal data to identify operational gaps and formulate actionable courses of action (COAs). Drafts executive correspondence and staff summary sheets for Space Delta 13 leadership and higher headquarters.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, the Under Secretaries of War, the Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel, Director of Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, the Chief Information Officer of the DoW, the Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Participates in and conducts strategic planning and analysis of key issues impacting DoW civilian human capital and workforce programs and priorities while maintaining cognizance of relevant human capital trends and best practices for Do W's civilian workforce. Analyzes and evaluates existing Department-level strategic guidance, including DoW issuances, and identifies potential areas for modifications. Identifies, defines and analyzes issues and problems in areas where precedents may not exist, or may be changing as directed by statute. Assists with major program studies and efforts around the President's Management Agenda, Strategic Management Plans and similar other strategic enterprise civilian human capital efforts. Analyzes and applies critical thinking to high-level administration policy, Congressional mandates, and DoW policy to develop recommendations for the DASW CPP and Department leadership on DoW civilian related strategy formulation, integration, and synchronization.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: 1) Applying extensive experience with Department of Air Force concepts, principles, practices, laws, regulations, policies, and precedents to provide comprehensive strategic advice and recommendations on complex organizational, operational, and mission-related matters; 2) Applying specialized expertise in Air Force law, policy, and instructions to analyze issues and provide guidance related to the Department of the Air Force as a force construct; 3) Analyzing military and civilian missions, organizational structures, work processes, and Department of the Air Force program goals and objectives to support strategic planning and decision-making; 4) Using advanced analytical and evaluative methods, together with a thorough understanding of the United States Air Force organizational structure, to assess complex programs, policies, operations, and organizational issues and develop recommendations for senior-level decision makers; 5) Identifying and resolving complex organizational and management problems characterized by significant breadth, importance, or severity, including situations in which established management techniques, policies, or procedures are insufficient. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of requirements, staff functions (including program management, staffing procedures, collaboration and coordination, Air Force Corporate Process, Strategic Planning and Programming System, etc.), the sequence and timing of key events and milestones, implementing policy and other actions, programming, and force structure as they apply to the organizational environment of the Department of Defense and the Department of the Air Force. Thorough understanding of military organization and commander issues sufficient to initiate, develop and drive strategic conference plans to support Air Force active duty, Air Reserve Component, Civilians, and Contractors. 2. Skills and ability to interpersonal emotional intelligence to engage with senior leaders and a planning team on a regular basis. Includes the ability to adapt and change course of action quickly, understand and interpret intent, and provide advice in a very concise and effective manner. Be able to engage and build trust with Senior Leaders at the highest level, thrive in a team environment as both a leader and a follower, display attention to detail, and possess strong organizational skills. Quickly assimilate and distill broad sets of information, and be comfortable working in complex, uncertain environments with minimal oversight. 3. Skills and ability to lead individuals and simultaneously manage multiple projects in a leadership capacity, and ability to perform any civilian responsibilities. Be able to engage in creative, actionable problem solving directly alongside SecAF, CSAF, DS and other principals to devise engagements that advance strategic objectives. 4. Ability to evaluate and assess conference and engagement effectiveness in all echelons of command, prepare reports on accomplishment of objectives, support a detailed integration effort, and developing recommendations while representing a wide variety of viewpoints and synthesizing complex, and often competing, information and viewpoints, to resolve issues, and to develop options and recommendations for senior Air Force leaders. 5. Skill in communicating effectively with tact and diplomacy, orally and in writing, to advocate positions; to respond to criticism of the organization's functions or performance; to explain programs, functions, and activities and gain understanding logically and effectively of the organization's efforts by concerned publics; and to negotiate effectively complex issues, programs, and functions with people having varying levels of understanding and to maintain good working relationships. 6. Skills and ability to independently manage short- and long-term projects and to cultivate and sustain positive working relationships to project completion. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Executing strategic reviews and participating in all phases of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) system; recommending program tradeoffs to balance budgets and resources; and monitoring component compliance with senior leadership. Preparing executive-level acquisition decision memoranda, reports, and interagency correspondence; reviewing annual defense authorization and appropriations acts or audit agency reports to ensure statutory compliance; and developing official responses to inquiries and testimony. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. Details.JobSummary: This position develops, analyzes, and coordinates A&S positions across the portfolio to align with strategic goals and Congressional mandates. The incumbent leads oversight to mitigate programmatic risks, such as unrealistic cost estimates, technical hurdles, and industrial base shortfalls. Additionally, the role integrates across the Department to provide assessments, support PPBE, and resolve emerging issues.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of War, Acquisition and Sustainment
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OUSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, the Under Secretaries of War, the Assistant Secretary of War, General Counsel, Director of Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, the Chief Information Officer of the DoW, the Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: This is a Direct Hire Public Notice, under this recruitment, applications will be accepted for each location and/or installation identified in this Public Notice and selections are made for vacancies as they occur. There may or may not be actual/projected vacancies at the time you submit your application. This Public Notice is to gather applications which may or may not result in a referral or selection. This position is being filled using Direct Hire Authority (DHA) authorized under the Department of War Civilian Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo) for position in the Business and Technical Management Professional Career Path (NH). Please read this Public Notice in its entirety prior to submitting your application for consideration. Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Leads the oversight of the assigned portfolio (Airlift, Tanker, and NC3) and identifies issues or potential issues, to include development of recommendations to address identified issues. Potential issues include unrealistic cost and schedule estimates; inadequate understanding and management of technical risk, unsound management practices, inappropriate acquisition strategies; immature technology and inadequate industrial base capabilities. Supports DoW's strategic reviews as directed with analysis of assigned mission capability portfolios with emphasis on mission capability gaps. This includes making critical recommendations on tradeoffs among programs within mission portfolios to buy the right things and balance the budget across Services and warfighting domains. Provides advice and staff support to the USW(A&S), ASW(A) and their teams with respect to operational analysis and mission gaps translated back to platform and weapon deficiencies, Science and Technology solution insertion points and concepts of employment, and Research and Development requirements for the future solution space and "to-be" systems architecture across appropriate mission areas. Develops and evaluates acquisition strategies, acquisition program baselines, analyses, risk reduction plans, international cooperation plans, and other applicable documentation for assigned major programs. Monitors the Services' compliance with and execution of Secretary of War, USW(A&S), or ASW(A) guidance and direction relating to assigned programs and activities. The incumbent shall guide the Services in understanding and complying with guidance and direction, exercising tact and understanding of organizational constraints. Where necessary, he/she shall formulate recommendations for further management action to ensure compliance or for modifications in cases where the guidance of direction has become infeasible or undesirable. Prepares and reviews correspondence and requests concerning assigned programs and activities directed to the SecWar the USW(A&S), the ASW(A), other agencies, the Office of the President, Legislative Branch offices, foreign governments or agencies, international organizations or private organizations or individuals. Prepares Acquisition Decision Memoranda, Overarching Integrated Product Teams (OIPT) reports, timely replies or action recommendations and other executive correspondence. Prepares and delivers program update briefings and coordinates program documentation.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the NH-IV level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-III (GS-13) grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to (1) Developing requirements and defining deliverables, project work plans, and performance metrics for complex technical contracts, specifically including advisory and assistance support, artificial intelligence (AI), and automation-focused contracts; and analyzing performance data to monitor contractor work execution; (2) Managing the financial portfolios of major acquisition programs, to include designing spend plans and tracking execution to support operational mission requirements; AND (3) Designing and recommending process improvements, standard operating procedures, and workflow modifications to optimize transaction accuracy, quality, and efficiency. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission.. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: The incumbent is responsible for analyzing and supporting the ASW (IBP) and Deputy Assistant Secretary of War Global Investment & Economic Security (GIES) regarding the development, execution, and monitoring of all GIES related acquisitions requirements. This position is responsible for also coordinating and collaborating with USW A&S Defense Business Office, Washington Headquarters Service Acquisition Directorate (WHS AD), and USW Office of General Counsel (OGC), among others.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of War, Acquisition and Sustainment (OUSW(A&S))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, the Under Secretaries of War, the Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel, Director of Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, the Chief Information Officer of the DoW, the Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: This is a Direct Hire Public Notice open only to current federal employees, under this recruitment, applications will be accepted for each location and/or installation identified in this Public Notice and selections are made for vacancies as they occur. There may or may not be actual/projected vacancies at the time you submit your application. This Public Notice is to gather applications which may or may not result in a referral or selection. This position is being filled using Direct Hire Authority (DHA) authorized under the Department of War Civilian Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo) for position in the Business and Technical Management Professional Career Path (NH). Please read this Public Notice in its entirety prior to submitting your application for consideration. Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: The incumbent is particularly responsible for the development of requirements and the monitoring of the advisory and assistance support contract, the technological artificial intelligence (AI) contracts, and the automation of multiple functions. The incumbent will define deliverables, structure project work plans, and provide leadership solutions to solve the most complex acquisitions and relevant financial processes. The incumbent will lead the development and execution of training of government personnel regarding the use of contracts for mission support. The incumbent will be responsible for the financial management of the acquisition portfolio, planning the spend plan, and ensuring GIES mission support. The incumbent has a general understanding of business processes across product lines and the ability to help design and recommend process changes, procedure redesigns, etc., as needed to support the IBP mission while assisting with quality efforts.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience include: 1) Applying regulations, policies, guidelines, and processes related to manpower, personnel, and services programs to provide program oversight, guidance, and recommendations; 2) Analyzing major manpower, personnel, and services issues, program goals and objectives, key events and milestones, and organizational roles to evaluate strategic plans, program requirements, and mission effectiveness; 3) Coordinating with major organizational elements, headquarters-level offices, and Department of Defense entities involved in the development, implementation, and oversight of services programs, strategic plans, and non-appropriated fund financial initiatives; 4) Evaluating organizational structures, missions, programs, and functional responsibilities to identify program requirements, resolve complex issues, and support enterprise-level services planning and execution. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of DoD and Air Force goals, objectives, and policies including knowledge of the relationship of the various Air Force entities involved in manpower, personnel, and services policies. 2. Knowledge of research and analysis techniques, problem resolution, and development of concrete action plans to solve problems. 3. Knowledge and skill in the application of Air Force workflow and task management directives, instructions, policies, procedures, and guidance. 4. Skill and ability to apply procedures, requirements, regulations, and policies related to specialized expertise in the work of the directorate, including the ability to maintain credibility with others on policy matters. 5. Ability to synthesize complex, and often competing, information and viewpoints to determine best course of action and advocate recommendations across the Air Staff and to senior Air Force leaders. 6. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing, negotiates complex issues, and maintains good working relationships. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Online Application: Questionnaire Resume: Your resume may NOT exceed two pages, and the font size should not be smaller than 10 pts. You will not be considered for this vacancy if your resume is illegible/unreadable. Additional information on resume requirements can be located under "How To Apply". Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15 form. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy of your most recent SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action, AND a SF-50 reflecting the highest grade held if different from your recent SF-50. The SF-50, block 24 must contain "1" or "2" AND block 34 must be a "1". Employees eligible under an OPM approved interchange agreement, block 34 may contain a "1" or "2". Promotion Consideration: If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirements. You will need to provide additional SF-50s which clearly demonstrates you meet the time-in-grade requirements (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Promotions, Within-Grade, Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s with an effective date more than one year old). ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form 214 must be submitted upon receipt. OPTIONAL DOCUMENTS: Performance Appraisals for Current Federal Civilian Employees - Most recent performance appraisals (dated within last 3 years) showing the official rating of record, signed by a supervisor, or statement why the performance appraisal is unavailable. Awards for Current Federal Civilian employees - List any awards received within the last 3 years on the resume. Note: Applicant must not submit award Notification of Personnel Actions (SF50s).

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Joint History and Research Office (JHRO), Office of the Director Joint Staff (ODJS)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS- 12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS 11 grade level in the Federal service: Applies organizational missions, roles, functions, and administrative policies of the Office of the Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Office of the Secretary of War, while actively applying a working knowledge of the missions, goals, and functions of other U.S. Government departments and agencies; Completing a wide range of administrative support functions to include maintaining a calendar, arranging meetings/briefings, coordinating appointments, entering travel requests, and arranging ground travel; Applying administrative and managerial regulations, policies and practices; the ability to formulate, implement guidance and apply new methods and procedures in administrative support, safety, supply accountability, travel, training, records management, publications and security; Applying evaluative and analytical methods to identify actions for proper dissemination to staff sections for appropriate action; to determine specific and implied tasks; and to negotiate reassignments of returned or unfavorable placement of taskings. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Substitution of education may not be used in lieu of specialized experience for this grade level.

Details.JobSummary: Part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The Administrative Operations Support Specialist is the sole civilian administrative support position within the JHRO. Employs a high-level of technical expertise to effectively monitor and maintain a dynamic schedule and ensure effective coordination of changes with numerous outside agencies. Provides for the effective management and coordination of a wide variety of complex and sensitive projects and action correspondence.
Details.SubAgencyName: Joint History and Research Office (JHRO), Office of the Director Joint Staff (ODJS)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: MISSION STATEMENT: The Joint History and Research Office supports the Executive Director for Joint History in the management of the Joint History Program, the provision of applied historical support to the CJCS and Joint Staff senior leaders, and the publishing of studies that document the activities of the Joint Force
MajorDuties: As an ADMINISTRATIVE OPERATIONS SUPPORT SPECIALIST at the GS-0301-12 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serving as principal point of contact for the Executive Director and refers matters for action and coordination to the appropriate branch Utilizing the Enterprise Task Management Software Solution (ETMS2) Responsible for the maintenance of the calendar, including coordinating attendance at, and arranging for hosting of all meetings/briefings, forecasting potential requirements, deconflicts problems, and plans and projects time for one time and historically recurring requirements In-processing of all assigned civilian and military personnel Ensuring appropriate liaison and coordination is conducted with key civilian and military officials within the Joint Staff or other departments and agencies as necessary

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S))
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The DCIPS occupational structure provides the foundation for managing the DCIPS pay structure. It consists of the following elements: mission categories, occupational groups, and work categories, work levels, pay band (for those DCIPS Components operating under the DCIPS pay banded structure using pay plan IA) and grades (for those DCIPS Components operating under the GG graded structure using pay plan GG), job titles, and competencies. You may qualify at the GG-13 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Qualifying experience would be demonstrated by 1) Providing guidance on the strategic oversight and the execution of Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), Privacy, Civil Liberties and Transparency (PCLT), and Records Management (RM) programs; 2) Formulating policy-based processes by analyzing information that influences these programs; and 3) Monitoring all phases of the data lifecycle pertaining to records management. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. It is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the length of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume? at https://www.usajobs.gov/Help/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include/ ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S)), Enterprise Administration and Management (EAM) Office. The Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (USW(I&S)) serves as the Principal Staff Assistant (PSA) and advisor to the Secretary of War (SecWar) regarding Intelligence; Counterintelligence (CI); DoW-wide Law Enforcement (LE) statute 10 USC 2672; and Security.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S))
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, Under Secretaries of War, Director of War Research and Engineering, Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, Assistants to the Secretary of War, Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: This Position is a Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1601 If selected, Federal employees currently serving in the competitive service must acknowledge that they will voluntarily leave the competitive service by accepting an offer of employment for a DCIPS excepted service positions. If selected, non-DCIPS candidates must acknowledge that the position they have been selected for is in the excepted service and covered by DCIPS. For more information see https://dcips.defense.gov/ Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as the Chief of Information Management providing strategic oversight and the execution of the organization's Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), Privacy, Civil Liberties and Transparency (PCLT), and Records Management (RM) programs. Independently monitors all phases of data lifecycle to include the collection, use, dissemination, disclosure and destruction of information within OUSW(I&S), ensuring strict alignment with federal statues and agency policies. Formulates and integrates policy-based processes, roles and controls governing organization wide data and records creation, collection, use, stored and disposition. Safeguards sensitive information while supporting accountability and transparency initiatives. Serves as the Component Records Management Officer (CRMO) ensuring compliance with Federal laws, policies, and records retention schedules across OUSW(I&S).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) Headquarters Space Force Command (HQSF) Force Design and Analysis (S9) at The Pentagon is searching for a Chief Analyst, Force Design Planning and Programming (NH-0343-04, GS 14/15 equivalent). Description: Help shape the future United States Space Force as the Chief Analyst for Force Design Planning and Programming. In this high-impact role, you will turn objective-force concepts, mission needs, and emerging technologies into practical, affordable investment recommendations. You will lead the integration of planning, programming, and cost information across Force Design field elements; represent shared priorities during Planning and POM activities; and ensure recommendations are analytically sound, well-documented, and aligned to enterprise needs. This is an ideal opportunity for a resource professional who enjoys solving complex problems, connecting strategic vision to executable programs, and influencing the decisions that modernize space capabilities. Each day, you will research and analyze data, assess investment options and transition plans, develop cost-informed recommendations within constrained resources, and help resolve funding issues across the Future Years Defense Program. You will prepare POM inputs, budget forecasts, unfunded requirement justifications, narratives, offsets, disconnects, reclamas, issue papers, briefings, and senior-leader decision packages. Success requires strong Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution experience; sound analytical judgment; comfort working independently in an evolving environment; and the ability to collaborate with headquarters staff, technical experts, acquisition organizations, and other stakeholders. Candidates who can communicate complex resource and force-design issues clearly, build consensus across competing priorities, and deliver timely, decision-ready products will thrive in this position. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate will possess substantial experience in Department of Defense PPBE and requirements processes, with demonstrated ability to develop Program Objective Memorandum inputs, budget forecasts, unfunded requirements justifications, POM narratives, offsets, disconnects, reclamas, and issue papers. Candidates should have a strong background in force planning, programming, resource analysis, and investment costing; experience evaluating funding profiles and resolving resource issues across the Future Years Defense Program; and familiarity with acquisition and long-range planning for space capabilities. The candidate should also bring strong qualitative and quantitative analytical skills, an ability to translate complex data into defensible recommendations, and experience preparing senior-leader briefings, reports, and decision packages. Experience working across military headquarters, technical teams, and other stakeholders to negotiate complex issues and integrate competing priorities is highly desirable. The position description does not identify a specific education requirement. Ten (10) or more years working in DoD operations, acquisitions, budget, and/or staff with preference in classified/special program space experience is highly desirable. Key Skills and Abilities: 1.Knowledge of the Department of Defense Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution System (PPBE) and Requirements processes. Understanding of procedures and schedules for developing Program Objective Memorandum (POM) inputs as well as methods for developing budget forecasts, unfunded requirements justifications, POM narratives, offsets and disconnects, reclamas, and issue papers. 2. Knowledge of military service program goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to actual events. 3. Knowledge of the relationship of the various military entities involved in overall planning and execution of military operations and evaluations and the methods in which the PPBE process supports them. 4. Knowledge of a wide range of qualitative and/or quantitative methods for the assessment and improvement of Space Force systems such as: Space Domain Awareness; Offensive and Defensive Space Operations; Positioning, Navigations, and Timing; Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance; Satellite Communications; Environmental Monitoring; Missile Warning; Space Operations; and Spacelift; and associated mission operations, test & training, or acquisition. 5. Ability to gather, assemble, and analyze facts, draw conclusions, conduct analysis, devise recommended solutions, and package the entire process in briefings, papers, or reports suitable for senior leader review and decision-making. 6. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing, negotiate complex issues, and maintain good working relations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the NH-4 (GS-14/15) level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the NH-3 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to NH-3. Experience 1) Overseeing and executing major construction and infrastructure programs, with a focus on energy resilience, cybersecurity, and facility modernization. 2) Directing data collection and in-depth analysis of facility and infrastructure requirements, developing and implementing policies and procedures related to cybersecurity for industrial control systems, and justifying program needs to senior officials and external stakeholders. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of War (OSW) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of War in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, fiscal, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSW includes the immediate offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of War, the Under Secretaries of War, the Assistant Secretaries of War, General Counsel, Director of Cost Assessment & Program Evaluation, Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, the Chief Information Officer of the DoW, the Director of Administration and Management, and such other staff offices as the Secretary establishes to assist in carrying out assigned responsibilities.
MajorDuties: This is a Direct Hire Public Notice, under this recruitment, applications will be accepted for each location and/or installation identified in this Public Notice and selections are made for vacancies as they occur. There may or may not be actual/projected vacancies at the time you submit your application. This Public Notice is to gather applications which may or may not result in a referral or selection. This position is being filled under Direct Hire Authority (DHA) in accordance with the AcqDemo Direct Hiring Authority (DHA) for acquisition and non acquisition positions involving 51% or more of time in direct support of acquisitions positions with Business and Technical Management Professional Career path. Please read this Public Notice in its entirety prior to submitting your application for consideration. Incumbents typical work assignments may include the following: Directs the development, collection of data, and in-depth analysis on Department of War (DoW) facility, infrastructure, and cyber requirements and resources, including foreign government cash funded and in-kind construction. Initiates programs, actions, and tasks to develop policies and procedures governing the cybersecurity of military infrastructure, facilities, facility and building control systems, and the secure operations of industrial control systems. Evaluates the impact of guidance and policies on existing conditions, procedures, and actions, analyzes program development, and makes recommendations for programming policy. Develops justifications to convince senior officials, Congress, and the public of the need to meet requirements at defense installations and improve their management. Fosters competition and creative thinking across Military Departments and Defense Agencies to provide excellent installations that support readiness and quality of life, including cyber-resilient infrastructure and modernized control systems.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-14 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Working knowledge of OSD, Joint Staff (JROC, JCB, FCBs) and COCOM organizations and Planning, Programming and Budget (PPBE) system/process at the Service Headquarters level, and broad understanding of the Navy program of record. Maintaining a high level of independent productivity and quality of work with a dynamic workload and staff as well as leading project/product teams and managing personnel administration. Providing experience with capability/requirements definition, documents and decision products for acquisition milestones while utilizing critical skills of written and oral communications, and demonstrated ability to brief, advise and provide recommendations to Flag Officers and Senior Executives. Demonstrating skills working with Navy and DoD requirements management and acquisition processes, while possessing the abilities in assessing, reviewing and drafting acquisition requirements, management policies and regulations. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY PROGRAM MANAGER in the INTEGRATED WARFARE DIVISION (N9I) of IMMEDIATE OFC OF CHIEF OF NVL OPS.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a key Navy expert through the Joint, Navy, and Urgent Requirements development phases in Navy and the OSW Program and Budget review.
You will supervise, direct and coordinate the daily operations of the branch of military, civilian, and/or contractor personnel.
You will execute a full range of supervisory and human resources functions for the Branch, including performance management, leadership and mentoring.
You will manage and coordinate the Navy implementation of the Joint Force Requirements Process (JFRP), to include serving as OPNAV's primary interface to the Joint Staff J8.
Details.Evaluations: In order to qualify for this position, your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the specific position for which you are being considered. Your resume is the key means we have for evaluating your skills, knowledge, and abilities as they relate to this position. Therefore, we encourage you to be clear and specific when describing your experience. When the application process is complete, we will review your resume to ensure you meet the hiring eligibility and qualification requirements listed in this announcement. You will be rated based on the information provided in your resume and application package, along with your supporting documentation to determine your ability to demonstrate the following competencies: Accountability Customer Service Decisiveness Flexibility Interpersonal Skills Problem Solving Resilience STRATEGIC THINKING ORAL COMMUNICATION PARTNERING PROBLEM SOLVING INFLUENCING/NEGOTIATING PLANNING AND EVALUATING This recruitment will utilize the following technical assessment tools: USA Hire AND Structured Interview. You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. All eligibility, qualifications, and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
Details.HowToApply: Please read the entire announcement and all the instructions before you begin an application. To apply and be considered for this position, you must complete all required questionnaires, assessments, and required documentation as specified in the How to Apply and Required Documents section. Resumes are restricted to no more than 2 pages. Illegible/unreadable resumes will not be considered. The complete application package must be submitted by 11:59 PM (ET) on the closing date of the announcement to receive consideration. The application process is as follows: 1. Click the Apply Online button. 2. Answer the questions presented in the application and attach all necessary supporting documentation. 3. Click the Submit Application button prior to 11:59 PM (ET) on the announcement closing date. 4. If you are required to complete any USA Hire Assessments, you will be notified after submitting your application. The notification will be provided in your application submission screen and via email. The notification will include your unique assessment access link to the USA Hire system and the completion deadline. Additionally, in USAJOBS you can click "Track this application" to return to your assessment completion notice. 5. Access USA Hire using your unique assessment link. Access is granted through your USAJOBS login credentials. 6. Review all instructions prior to beginning your assessments. You will have the opportunity to request a testing accommodation before beginning the assessments should you have a disability covered under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended. 7. Set aside at least 2 hours to take the USA Hire assessments; however, most applicants complete the assessments in less time. If you need to stop the assessments and continue later, you can re-use your unique assessment link. 8. Your responses to the USA Hire Assessments will be reused for one year (in most cases) from the date you complete an assessment. If future applications you submit require completion of the same assessments, your responses will be automatically reused. Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request a RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments if you received the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need a RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments here: https://appsupport.usastaffing.gov/hc/en-us/sections/28980686389652-Reasonable-Accommodation-Information For more general information, system requirements and to request assistance regarding the USA Hire Assessments, review the following resources: https://support-usahire.opm.gov/hc/en-us To update your application, including supporting documentation: During the announcement open period, return to your USAJOBS account, find your application record, and click Edit my application. This option will no longer be available once the announcement has closed. To view the announcement status or your application status: Click on this: https://help.usajobs.gov/how-to/application/status. Your application status page is where you can view your application status, USA Hire assessment completion status, and review your notifications sent by the hiring agency regarding your application. You are encouraged to apply online. Applying online will allow you to review and track the status of your application. Do not email or send hard copy resumes/applications to the Contact Information or Agency Information listed in this vacancy announcement. All resumes/applications received at the addresses listed in the Contact Information or Agency Information will be destroyed and will not be considered for this vacancy announcement. It is the applicant's responsibility to verify that all information in their resume and documents are legible and accurate. HR will not modify answers/documents submitted by an applicant.
Details.WhatToExpectNext: When the application process is complete, your complete application will be reviewed to determine if you meet the hiring eligibility and qualification requirements for which you requested consideration. Details.RequiredDocuments: You are required to provide documentation that supports the eligibility and qualification claims made in your resume. You must submit the applicable documents listed here and those listed with the eligibilities you select in the announcement questionnaire with your application package. Applicants who do not provide supporting documentation that fully support their claims will not be referred to the hiring manager. Cover letter is optional. A complete resume is required. Resumes are restricted to no more than 2 pages. Illegible/unreadable resumes will not be considered. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week if experience was less than full time (35-40 hours per week), and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience. TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you applying for a promotion? For GS positions, to be considered for promotion, you must provide SF-50(s) that shows you held the next lower GS grade for at least one year. SF-50s that have an effective date within the past year (e.g., General Adjustment SF-50 from this year or Within Rate/Grade Increases (WRI/WGI) SF-50 within a year) do not clearly show that you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirement. That means if you submit an SF-50 dated within the last year, you must submit another SF-50 that is dated more than one year ago to clearly demonstrate you meet the time-in-grade requirements. If you are a DoD employee, you can obtain a copy of your SF- 50(s) from MyBiz. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference? If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Application documents, including supplemental ones, may be shared outside the Human Resources Office. Supplemental documents may contain your SSN, DOB, or personal information of others (e.g., on military orders, marriage certificates). You may redact this information before submitting; however, if selected, you must provide unredacted originals.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) Headquarters Space Force Command (HQSF) at The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia is searching for a Senior Data Specialist to support S5SB (NH-0343-04, GS 14/15 equivalent). Description: The USSF Force Structure Division (S5F) within the Deputy CSO for Strategy, Plans, Programs and Requirements (HQSF/S5/8) is responsible for assessing the current "Programmed Force," analyzing the gap to the future "Objective Force," and conducting the annual multi-service Space Risk Assessment. The USSF Senior Data Analyst will be a foundational expert in this division, responsible for providing the data-driven insights that inform the Space Force's most critical strategy, requirements, and resourcing decisions. The selectee will gather, clean, and analyze force structure data from across the DoD; employ dynamic analytic tools to identify trends, gaps, and risks; and, most importantly, translate complex findings into defendable briefings and compelling visualizations for senior leaders. This position requires the maturity and poise to conduct senior action officer responsibilities on a 4-star level staff. The ideal candidate is an expert in data analysis who can thrive in a collaborative environment, working with mission area experts, operators, and planners. Ability to employ advanced data analysis tools that leverage data obtained from model-based systems engineering methods a must. Knowledge of AI/LLMs for data assessment and report generation is highly desired. Experience with modeling and simulation tools and knowledge of mission engineering principles are preferred but not required. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate will have a background in data analysis, operations research, program analysis, or a related field, with experience working in a Department of Defense operational or headquarters environment. They must be a skilled staff officer capable of synthesizing information from multiple sources and presenting data-driven recommendations. The ability to assess complex data and translate the outcomes into effective visualizations and written/oral communications is essential. The candidate must be skilled and comfortable with a range of software applications, including Microsoft Office suite of tools (e.g., Excel and PowerPoint), and should have experience with more advanced data analysis tools (e.g., Python, R, SQL, Tableau, Qlik). Experience with modeling and simulation tools or as a developer is preferred but not required. Knowledge of Mission Engineering is desired but not required. Key Skills and Abilities: 1. The candidate will have a background in data analysis, operations research, program analysis, or a related field, with experience working in a Department of Defense operational or headquarters environment. They must be a skilled staff officer capable of synthesizing information from multiple sources and presenting data-informed and derived recommendations for Space Force senior leadership decision-making. 2. The candidate must be skilled and comfortable with a range of software applications, including Microsoft Office suite of tools, and should have knowledge of appropriate application of more advanced data analysis tools (e.g., Python, SQL, Tableau, Qlik) for assessing complex data and translating the outcomes into effective visualizations. 3. The candidate will have extensive knowledge and skill in qualitative and qualitative methods for assessing force structure as it pertains to the appropriate mix, size, and composition of forces, capabilities, and infrastructure required to meet strategic objectives and operational demands. 4. The candidate will possess the ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing; negotiate complex issues; and maintain good working relations. 5. The candidate will have the ability to work with partners outside the Space Force to include foreign allies and partners.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the GS-15 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your experience: Overseeing the production, quality control, and routing of highly sensitive executive correspondence, decision memos, and briefing material; and Providing senior level direction in performing a variety of highly complex assignments including analyzing and evaluating major organizational initiatives (such as managing resource execution, establishing operational policies). Utilizing an enterprise-level task and correspondence management system (such as the Correspondence and Task Management System (CATMS), TMT, or ETMS2) to assign, track, suspense, and report on high-priority executive actions and leadership decisions. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Immediate Office (IO) of the Director, Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) and serves as the Business Operations Manager in support of the Director and Deputy Director. The incumbent is considered a recognized authority on the full spectrum of WHS operational issues.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), Department of War (DOW) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as Business Operations Manager and Senior Advisor, providing executive-level program management, controlling administrative actions and resource execution, and advising the WHS Director and Deputy Director on complex, cross-functional organizational and operational issues. Exercises full supervisory and personnel management responsibilities, directing a professional staff by assigning workloads, evaluating performance (DPMAP/EPAT), resolving complaints, identifying training needs, and fostering a high-performance, EEO-compliant environment. Directs day-to-day business operations and executive correspondence, utilizing the Correspondence and Task Management System (CATMS) to track suspenses, providing quality control for decision instruments and briefing packages submitted to the Secretary of War (SecWar), DA&M, and WHS leadership in accordance with DoD Manual 5110.04. Leads business process re-engineering and continuous process improvement initiatives, applying advanced qualitative and quantitative methodologies to evaluate program effectiveness, optimize the use of limited resources across the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) lifecycle, and generate innovative workflow solutions. Develops and enforces administrative and operational policies, overseeing official records management (NARA compliance), time and attendance (DAI), and property accountability, while representing WHS in executive-level working groups to resolve contentious issues and integrate organizational goals.
